title: Punches
description: Records from the Hikvision clocks. They are copied every 5 minutes.

messages.notConfigured: The API has no clock user (CHECADOR_USER or TIME_CLOCK_USER): nothing is synced.
messages.withoutClocks: No time clocks have been added yet.

messages.error: A clock failed on its last sync; see which one below.
messages.pending: The first sync has not finished yet.

status.offlineText: Check that it is on and connected to the network. The punches are still stored in the clock and will be copied when it reconnects.

clock.pending: Its first sync has not finished yet.

sync.hint: Pulls everything still missing from each clock (the full backlog). Runs in the background; you can keep using the system.
sync.alreadyRunning: Every clock is already syncing; wait for them to finish.

import.hint: Pulls every punch in the selected date range from all the clocks. It may take several minutes; you can keep using the system.

otherHint: Not a valid punch (device code {{minor}}). It does not count for attendance.

errors.status: Could not load the time clock status

report.title: Attendance
report.description: Shifts built from the time clock punches and matched to each employee by their time clock number.
report.withoutLink: The {{count}} unlinked ones show the time clock name and the “Not linked” mark.
report.rule: The time clock does not tell entries from exits: punches alternate, repeats within 5 min are ignored and a shift lasts at most 13 h.

employees.title: Time clock employees
employees.description: Match each time clock number to its system user. The clock prefixes the area to the number (070562 = payroll 562), so the link is confirmed here.

kpis.hintWithoutLink: Their punches come out with no person
kpis.hintSuggestions: They can be linked in one go

risk.title: {{count}} not linked
risk.text: Unlinked numbers do not build workdays: in the report they show up with the clock number and the "Not linked" mark. Review them so everyone has their entries and exits.

differences.title: Differences
differences.description: Reconcile the clock numbers with the system's people. Pick a number and then who it belongs to; nothing is saved until you confirm.
differences.readOnly: Read-only: you lack the permission to link. You can see the differences, but not assign.
differences.summary: {{missing}} not linked · {{free}} people with no number in the clock

people.title: From the system
people.empty: Everyone already has a number in the clock.

action.pickPerson: and then the person it belongs to
action.assignedWarning: {{name}} is already assigned to {{number}}; it can also be assigned to this number.

errors.load: Could not read the clock employees
errors.people: Could not load the system's people

clocks.title: Time clocks
clocks.description: Add the time clocks and check their configuration and sync. The system only reads from the clocks.
clocks.readOnly: Read-only: the system connects to the clocks to read their punches and configuration; it never changes anything on them. Only punches (face, fingerprint or card) are read, not door openings.
clocks.credentials: It connects with the clock user and password configured in the API (the same for every clock).
clocks.notConfigured: The API has no clock user: set CHECADOR_USER and CHECADOR_PASS (or TIME_CLOCK_USER and TIME_CLOCK_PASS) in the server's .env and recreate the container; it cannot connect to any clock.
clocks.empty: No time clocks have been added yet.

usage.hint: If it counts, its punches build the shifts together with the other clocks that count: the first punch of the shift is the entry and the last one the exit, whatever the clock (people may enter through one and leave through another). If it does not count, its punches are stored and shown in the table, but not used for entries/exits or overtime.

config.title: Clock configuration
config.hint: Read live from the clock, without changing anything.
config.name: Name on the clock
config.peopleItem: {{withFace}} with face · {{withFingerprint}} with fingerprint · {{withCard}} with card
config.driftHint: Set the time on the clock itself (preferably with NTP). If the clocks disagree, an entry on one and an exit on another add or remove worked time.

dialog.urlHint: The IP or the address you open in the browser to log into the clock.
dialog.name: Name (optional)
dialog.nameHint: Leave it empty to use the name configured on the clock.
dialog.registrationNote: The system connects to confirm the address and starts pulling its punches. It does not change the clock.
dialog.retirementText: It stops syncing. Its punches stay and, if you add it again, it resumes where it left off. It does not change the clock.
dialog.editNote: It only changes how the system uses this clock's punches. It does not change the clock.

toasts.registration: {{name}} added: it is already pulling its punches

errors.status: Could not read the clocks status
errors.config: Could not read the clock configuration

write.label: Allow writing to this clock
write.hint: When on, the system can add, remove and register fingerprints on this clock. When off, the clock is read-only for the system.

history.title: {{name}} history
history.empty: No sync attempts recorded for this clock yet.
history.loadError: The history could not be read; please try again.
history.read: {{new}} new punches out of {{read}} events checked
history.hint: The system only reads from the clocks. A failed attempt loses nothing: the device keeps the punches and the next round brings them.

roster.title: Clock roster
roster.description: People on the clocks that count for entries and exits. What is on the clock is reviewed here; nobody is removed without a reason.

form.reasonHint: At least {{min}} characters. Saved in the audit log.
